description: Which modulus IMPOWER takes (review of CR-321578802, rounds 1 and 2, reviewer 1 B1). Near |z| = 1 (A1:A10, each base raised to the 50000000th power): A1:A3 tell the correctly rounded hypot from the logarithms' modulus, A4:A6 the correctly rounded from x86_64 glibc's, A7:A9 tell it from both, A10 from a full x87 chain. Away from 1 (A11:A16) the two families differ outright: the logarithms' modulus forms the double sum of the squares, each square 0 when it is subnormal, where a hypot keeps the base's size. A11:A14 have a zero modulus: in A11, A12 and A14 the squares themselves round to 0, and A14's negative power makes it #NUM!; in A13 each square (1E-320) is subnormal but not 0, so the modulus is 0 by the flush, where the IEEE sum (2E-320) is not 0. A15:A16 flush only the smaller square (1E-308): the sum (about 1.01E-306) is normal, so the modulus stays nonzero but changes, to 1E-153 where |z| is about 1.005E-153. A17 is IMSQRT of A15's base, evidenced already (probes/eng-imln-modulus-range A80). A18:A23 are the cells of review round 3 (reviewer 1 N1) that the rest does not cover: A18 is an ordinary base at a small power, where the families differ in the 15th digit; A19 has both squares subnormal and a normal sum, so the logarithms' modulus is 0 by the flush alone; A20 is the same shape with each square just normal, where both agree; A21 is the power 0 of a zero modulus, #NUM! where a hypot gives 1; A22 and A23 are a pure real and a pure imaginary base with a subnormal square, which the logs never flush and IMSQRT does.
